outlook: Wheat led a Monday rebound after last week's selloff, up about 12 cents in Chicago as Russia said it would step up strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure, raising Black Sea export worries. Soybeans recovered about 7 cents from near five-week lows, though StoneX raised its U.S. crop estimate above USDA's September number. Corn is barely higher just under $5, still weighed down by large Sept. 1 stocks (2.095 billion bu) and slow export sales, while canola is flat. Improving harvest weather is expected this week, and USDA's WASDE and Crop Production reports come Friday.
